RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own — it's a common outcome in senior news management and proves nothing about this decision. Don't lead with it. It matters mainly as a procedural point: many public broadcasters have their own guidelines on balanced panels, so check whether yours were breached. That's a concrete failing you can cite.

Your stronger ground is elsewhere. Chase the written reasons formally — a two-week silence from a public body is itself a problem, and ask in writing. Then check whether "strong digital experience" appeared in the original criteria and person specification. If it was added afterwards, that's the real question. If it was always there, the decision may simply be defensible.
